name: Lethlor Ravine
summary: Lethlor Ravine is a jagged, rocky canyon winding through the eastern reaches of the Badlands. It serves as a perilous roost and breeding ground for the black dragonflight, swarming with aggressive whelps and mature drakes.

sections.title: A Dragonflight's Bastion
sections.body: Carved deep into the scorched plateaus of the eastern Badlands, Lethlor Ravine is one of the most hazardous stretches of the desert. The craggy canyon walls provide a natural aerie for the black dragonflight, housing nests of fierce dragon whelps guarded by larger, fire-breathing drakes. Few travelers dare approach the valley floor, as the shadows overhead constantly betray the flight of winged predators circling among the rocky spires.

sections.title: Mysteries in the Dust
sections.body: Beyond the scaly brood that claims it, Lethlor Ravine is marked by curious crystalline obelisks scattered throughout the crags. These crystalline formations are involved in a local quest chain. Their origin is not established.

faq.answer: Lethlor Ravine is a deep, craggy canyon located on the eastern side of the Badlands, functioning primarily as a nesting ground for black dragons.

faq.q: Why are there so many black dragons here?
aliases: why are there dragons in badlands
faq.answer: The black dragonflight uses the sheltered, desolate rock formations of Lethlor Ravine to roost and rear their young, turning the canyon into a fortified nursery far away from major civilized cities.

faq.q: What are the crystal obelisks in the ravine?
faq.answer: The crystalline obelisks are formations scattered throughout the ravine and involved in a local quest chain. Their origin is not established.

faq.q: Is Lethlor Ravine safe for travelers?
aliases: can i walk through lethlor ravine
faq.answer: No. The ravine is extremely dangerous, filled with flying drakes and aggressive whelps that attack trespassers on sight.

angles.text: The skies and ridges of Lethlor Ravine provide a stern test of marksmanship against fast-moving dragonkin and winged predators.
